The first release with a native Windows build, next to the Linux one.

**Downloads**

- `qwfnfer-windows-x86_64-cuda.zip`: Windows 10/11 x64. Unzip it anywhere and run `qwfnfer.cmd`. It carries the engine, the console, ggml (every CPU variant; CUDA for Turing to Blackwell), the CUDA 13.4 runtime and the Visual C++ runtime, so there is nothing to install but the NVIDIA driver (580 or newer) and Python 3.
- `qwfnfer-linux-x86_64-cuda.zip`: as before; `scripts/install.sh` installs it. glibc 2.35 or newer.
- `SHA256SUMS` for both.

**On Windows, for full speed** (README, FAQ, *Windows?*): set the NVIDIA Control Panel's *CUDA - Sysmem Fallback Policy* to *Prefer No Sysmem Fallback* for `bin\qwfn-server.exe`, turn on hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling, and keep the model files off a BitLocker-encrypted volume.

**Changes since v0.2.3**

- Windows support (#2 by @HyperRamzey, brought onto master in #16): one I/O worker pool for both systems, over unbuffered overlapped reads on Windows; the VRAM expert tier is sized from the free memory the driver reports, so it never spills silently into shared system memory; the engine opts out of Windows 11 power throttling.
- The engine never runs more CPU threads than the machine has. The default of 8 on a machine with fewer logical CPUs made every CPU graph wait on descheduled threads: 50x slower decode on the CPU in the worst case measured.
- #10: stall-probe deadlock, prefill-aware stall watchdog, reset after a failed generation, equal-prompt reuse, direct-I/O alignment. #12: the sparse attention's prefill block selection. #13: llama.cpp pinned by commit. #14: io_uring reaping and request accounting (with a further fix for a rejected request counted on the thread-pool backend).
- The server reads text files, and zip archives of them, attached to a chat (OpenAI `file` parts, Anthropic `document` blocks).
- The console's tune names a GPU whose PCIe link runs below its width or generation.
- CI on Linux and Windows checks the engine against llama.cpp, token for token, on a tiny random model with every tensor of the architecture; each release zip is unpacked and run on a machine with no GPU before it is published.
